description: Line-granular freeze: a context substring that over-matches would silently subtract a renameable DevFlow from the baseline; the reverse stale-check only catches a context matching nothing, not one over-matching. No live defect (all current contexts target single-DevFlow lines); author-error fail-open.

A frozen.occurrences entry naming a file also in a whole-file frozen bucket is silently inert (classify returns at the first whole-file match) yet the reverse stale-check does not flag it; dead configuration reading as active.

The #2003 provenance-test comment leans toward derivation ('Without the per-line value exclusion...'), restating what the assertion already proves; closest of the block's comments to the prevention-only comment standard's edge.
The reverse-check's unreadable/absent-file OSError arm (distinct finding string + continue) is untested; a refactor could silently drop it.
A context matching multiple brand-bearing lines (multi-line accumulation in occurrence_frozen_count) is never exercised; all tests use single-line contexts.
Multiple frozen.occurrences rows for one file (occ_file_map setdefault/append aggregation) is exercised only by the real-tree gate, not a focused synthetic test.
The per-line max(c,0) clamp is dead-defensive (PROVENANCE_VALUE matches per line can never exceed the brand count); noted as unreachable, no test recommended.

Line-granular freeze despite 'per-occurrence' framing: a future line carrying both a must-keep and a renameable DevFlow would over-freeze the renameable one. Docstring accurately describes the line-granular behavior; no live defect. (Corroborates silent-failure-hunter's over-freeze suggestion.)
